They prove idempotent suspend/resume, initially hidden attachment, local R7 preview scheduler cancellation and restart without wall-time debt, and unchanged current combat behavior. The first canonical browser phase retained 17 passes and one real lifecycle failure: Phaser pause suppressed updates but left request-animation-frame callbacks scheduled. The first run passed import, types, work packages 72/72, combat 48/48, Practice 4/4, identity 22/22, reward 28/28 and protocol 21/21, then preserved a tooling inventory failure. Updating the expected current Practice inventory passed the exact tooling file 31/31. reviews.details: Direct review traced normal startup, page visibility/pagehide/pageshow ordering, Phaser scheduling, current R7 local and server-backed presentation, Socket.IO manual reconnect, session bootstrap, V10 fresh-snapshot input fencing, disconnect movement release and Daily resume. Hidden state cancels transient projection, stops both Phaser and local preview schedulers and disconnects the socket. Resume resets timer anchors, reconnects the same bounded server authority and never enables input from stale projection. No gameplay, server timing, replay, Daily limit, PEI, reward, helper, database, asset, dependency or environment behavior changed. Physical Android power attribution remains Phone Gate A.

Performance and visual phases were not selected: the change adds no pixels and the focused browser proof counts the exact hidden scheduler and snapshot work that caused the power risk. Foreground physical smoothness remains part of Phone Gate A.
PostgreSQL was not selected because lifecycle hardening changes no database, store, migration, settlement or concurrency boundary.
The daily/release suite was not run because this is a feature waypoint before physical Phone Gate A rather than the 22:00 checkpoint or an explicit release boundary.
Physical Android/iOS and Nimiq Pay battery acceptance has not run yet; Phone Gate A is the only remaining package gate.
